rules.text: The goal is single neurons; there is no multi-unit category. A cluster that looks neuronal but has too much waveform variability or contamination to accept as one unit, and whose tree shows dense components, should be SPLIT until a single unit emerges. A cluster that is too broad, too contaminated for its spike count and unlikely to contain a valid unit should be DISCARDED. A small leftover at the end of splitting that resembles no other cluster should be DISCARDED.

Several dense components in the tree, each made of many subclusters, suggest several embedded units; split towards them. A large spike count, many leaves or a complex tree alone is not a reason to split. Stop splitting when the part in hand is a single unit.

Before choosing SPLIT, look at the split preview. Different waveform families and a cross-correlogram without a refractory gap support splitting. Similar waveforms and a refractory gap in the cross-correlogram mean the two parts are one unit; do not split them apart only for that reason when the cluster's own autocorrelogram is clean. When the cluster's own ±2 ms zone is filled, the contamination is inside the parts, so SPLIT further (S4).

The refractory gap in the autocorrelogram is the primary unit criterion. Judge how much the ±2 ms zone is filled relative to the shoulders rather than applying a fixed number, and read contamination estimates relative to the spike count; hill_contamination 0.5 means saturated (at least half contaminated), not a borderline value. A cluster whose ±2 ms zone is partly or fully filled is not yet a single unit: SPLIT it while SPLIT is offered (gate G2), and judge KEEP or DISCARD only for clean parts or when SPLIT is no longer offered.

Typical signs of noise: a triangular or strongly periodic autocorrelogram; waveforms that do not look like spikes; more than three phases, a monophasic shape, a slow descent to the trough, a start far from baseline or an overly broad waveform; units mixed with noise that cannot be split further.

Judge morphology as a whole. A biphasic or triphasic shape is compatible with a neuron but does not certify one; one extra bump or an endpoint away from zero is not enough to call noise; there is no universal width cutoff.
State the observed evidence for noise. Do not turn every uncertain cluster into KEEP or into SPLIT.
Amplitude over time should be roughly stable; bursting units may vary. Inspect periods of abrupt change for noise.
A low-rate cluster with an empty autocorrelogram should first be considered for merging; discard it only if it resembles no other cluster.
Spike count and leaf count are not labels. There is no fixed minimum cluster size and no target number of units; the leftover rule in S1 is the only size-related judgement.

MERGE needs all of: the same waveform shape, the same amplitude (one cluster about twice the other or more, see amplitude_ratio, is not the same unit even when the shapes match), an empty ±2 ms zone in the cross-correlogram, amplitudes that continue into each other or share one band over time, and no clear rise in violations after merging (isi_violation_increase). A null contamination_increase means the estimate is saturated, not that nothing changes. A high correlation is only the reason this pair was asked about.
Amplitudes that continue into each other over time, one cluster fading as the other appears, are strong evidence of one drifting neuron split into two clusters.

A peak at about 5-10 ms on one side of the cross-correlogram only, with the ±2 ms zone empty and a smaller second spike, indicates bursts of one unit and supports merging (label burst_peak_5_10ms). A sharp peak at or next to zero lag is not a burst: it fills the refractory zone and argues against merging (label zero_lag_peak; see ccg_zero_lag_ratio). A weak, symmetric cross-correlogram also argues against merging.
DISCARD only on evidence that the source itself is noise. Small size, low correlation or not matching this target is not enough.
NOT_MERGE does not certify that the source is clean.
Judge the source's validity the same way whichever target it is compared with. Never merge or discard to reach a cluster count.

Identical waveforms with a filled ±2 ms zone in the cross-correlogram are not a reason to DISCARD the source; choose NOT_MERGE. Merging and then splitting does not separate them here, because SPLIT only undoes the last merge.

A target that is itself heavily contaminated (target_contamination saturated at 0.5, a filled ±2 ms zone in the merged autocorrelogram) is a mixture still to be split, not a destination; do not merge small clusters into it on waveform similarity alone.

gates.text: MERGE stands only if your labels are overlay similar, ccg refractory_clean or burst_peak_5_10ms, amplitude_time continuous_or_handoff or overlapping_same_level, and source_validity valid; otherwise the harness records NOT_MERGE.
When SPLIT is offered, KEEP stands only if your refractory label is not partly_contaminated or absent; otherwise the harness records SPLIT.
